# Objective

Apply the user-confirmed round-4 disposition (2026-10-22): the ambiguous
Phred+64 signature window (whole-file every byte >= 64 and some >= 90) stops
being a hard error and becomes a per-dataset `QUALITY_ENCODING_AMBIGUOUS`
WARNING finding that forces the group to REVIEW. Bytes outside ASCII [33, 126]
still abort (provable violation). No encoding-declaration machinery, no data
modification advice, no Phred+64 support (v1 is Phred+33 only).

# Rationale (confirmed)

The signature is valid under BOTH encodings (Cock et al. 2010: Sanger FASTQ
encodes Q0-93 as ASCII 33-126), so a hard rejection asserts a guess — the same
pretense the spec forbids ("do not pretend ASCII ranges can distinguish").
Ambiguity withholds automatic approval (REVIEW) but never blocks the report,
mirroring the uncalibrated-threshold philosophy.

# Scope

1. `models.FastqFileStats.encoding_ambiguous: bool = False` (per strand;
   dataset-level ambiguity = any strand flagged).
2. `fastq.StrandStats.finalize()` sets the flag instead of raising; module
   docstring and constant comments updated; the hard [33, 126] byte check is
   untouched.
3. `policy._metadata_findings` emits one WARNING finding per affected dataset
   (both readings named; metrics computed under Phred+33; resolution is
   verifying the source encoding — never modifying data) and sets metadata
   REVIEW, so `QUALITY_ENCODING_AMBIGUOUS` reaches the decision reason codes.
4. README encoding section rewritten: abort range, ambiguous-warns semantics,
   Cock et al. citation, no override flag.
5. Tests: `test_likely_phred64_rejected` becomes an ambiguity-flag test;
   scan-level flag tests; e2e test asserting REVIEW + reason code + finding.

# Verification

1. Unit: uniform-`]` file scans with `encoding_ambiguous=True`; mixed and
   uniform-`K` files stay `False`; byte-out-of-range still aborts.
2. e2e: group containing one ambiguous dataset → metadata REVIEW, decision
   REVIEW (exit 1), finding and reason code present.
3. Full suite green; mypy and ruff clean. Examples unchanged (none use the
   ambiguous window). No benchmark impact (no hot-path change).
